input.quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
input.rationale: The cap is nominally mutual but the basis is far below the playbook position: it is limited to amounts "actually paid" (not paid or payable) by Corio and only for "the transaction which the liability relates to", so Commerce One's exposure could be a small fraction of 12 months' fees and there is no US$1,000,000 floor. Carve-outs are limited to Section 8 (Commerce One's IP indemnity, which benefits us and is retained); there are no carve-outs for confidentiality/data protection and security breaches (Section 10), gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and Corio's payment obligations are not excluded from the cap. Redline changes the basis to the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, keeps mutuality, and adds one "Excluded Claims" sentence placing indemnities, confidentiality/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap and the consequential-damages waiver. Fallback: straight 12 months' fees with those carve-outs.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap a meaningful mutual amount (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000) and add standard uncapped carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have reset the cap to the greater of twelve (12) months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000, in place of the amount "actually paid ... for the transaction which the liability relates to", which is too narrow to be a meaningful remedy. Consistent with our playbook, indemnification, confidentiality/data protection and security breaches, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Corio's payment obligations are not treated as capped damages; if helpful, we can accept a straight 12 months' fees cap with those carve-outs retained.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE LIABILITY AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (US$1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT OR ITS OTHER INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; CORIO'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS SECTION 9.
